Paraszczak, J., Svedlund, E., Fytas, K. and Laflamme, M. (2014). Electrification of Loaders and Trucks - A Step Towards More Sustainable Underground Mining. International Conference on Renewable Energies and Power Quality (ICREPQ'14), Cordoba, Spain, 8-10 April 2014. Renewable Energy and Power Quality Journal, Vol. 1, No. 12, pp. 81-86. https://doi.org/10.24084/repqj12.240

Locators are printed journal page numbers (81-86; PDF page = printed - 80). A 6-page qualitative review of battery, cable (tethered), trolley and hybrid electric LHDs and trucks for deep underground metal mines. Few technology numbers: diesel power-train efficiency 30-35 % and electric drive ~90 % (Sect. 2, generic), unit sizes (payloads, motor and auxiliary diesel kW for the Kiruna EMT-35/EMT-50), state of development, and hybrid LHD prototype fuel reduction 10 % (entered as CO2 ERP). No absolute energy per tonne or per hour, no equipment prices. Relative figures (trolley truck uses 24 % of diesel-fleet energy per t hauled, cable LHD opex 10-30 % lower, energy cost share 15 % vs 5 %, trolley infrastructure ~75 % of truck price, battery 4 h per charge) are in _other-values and _measures. Cable-LHD economics are reprinted from InfoMine 2012 and the authors' CIM Journal 2013 paper. Technology names: haul-truck_electric-drive (generic electric drive), loader_cable-electric and haul-truck_trolley-electric (full trolley, not trolley-assist) are composed names.
